explanations.explanation: Hold on, friend, nobody is palming this scroll. Zechariah says it's "twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide." (Zechariah 5:2) That's way too big for one hand, even with a mustache helping. It's a huge scroll, and it's flying.

Right, friend. Zechariah answers the angel, "I see a flying scroll… twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide." (Zechariah 5:2) That's far too big to hold in one hand. I can't even keep a small cookie box steady, and this thing is up in the air.

Yes, friend. The angel says, "This is the curse that is going out over the face of all the land." (Zechariah 5:3) Then he says what it does: every thief will be removed, and every perjurer too. A perjurer is someone who swears falsely. This scroll is serious.

I get the pull of that word, because blessing sounds so much nicer. But the angel says, "This is the curse that is going out over the face of all the land." (Zechariah 5:3) It's aimed at thieves and perjurers, who will be removed. This one's a curse, friend.

A census is a head count, so I see where your mind went with a big scroll full of writing. But the angel says, "This is the curse that is going out over the face of all the land." (Zechariah 5:3) Nobody's being counted here. Wrongdoers are being removed.

That's it, friend. The angel says one side is for "every thief" and the other is for "every perjurer." (Zechariah 5:3) A perjurer is someone who swears falsely. Verse 4 says it's the one who "swears falsely by My name."

Idols are a serious matter in the Bible, but they aren't what this scroll names. The angel says one side is for "every thief" and the other is for "every perjurer." (Zechariah 5:3) A perjurer is someone who swears falsely. Verse 4 says it's the one who "swears falsely by My name."

explanations.answer: Everyone who works on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: That one sounds believable, friend, but it's not on this scroll. The angel says one side is for "every thief" and the other is for "every perjurer." (Zechariah 5:3) A perjurer is someone who swears falsely. The Sabbath doesn't come up in this passage.

Yes, friend. The LORD of Hosts says, "I will send it out… and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by My name. It will remain inside his house and destroy it." (Zechariah 5:4) It goes in and it stays. I hope nobody's wishing it would just pop in and leave.

Close, but it does stay. The LORD of Hosts says it will enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by His name. Then He says, "It will remain inside his house and destroy it." (Zechariah 5:4) No quick visit here, friend. It remains.

explanations.answer: Destroys it down to its timbers and stones
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The LORD of Hosts says it "will remain inside his house and destroy it, down to its timbers and stones." (Zechariah 5:4) Timbers are the wooden beams. Nothing is left standing. That's a thorough job.

explanations.answer: Marks its door so everyone will know
explanations.explanation: A mark on the door is a neat idea, friend, but the text never says it. The LORD of Hosts says the curse "will remain inside his house and destroy it, down to its timbers and stones." (Zechariah 5:4) It works from the inside. The timbers and stones go with it.

explanations.answer: Hands it over to a brand new owner
explanations.explanation: No new owner moves in here, friend. The LORD of Hosts says the curse "will remain inside his house and destroy it, down to its timbers and stones." (Zechariah 5:4) Nobody gets the keys. The house is destroyed.
You got it, friend. The angel says, "A measuring basket is going forth." (Zechariah 5:6) It's a basket, not a jar or a chest. And what's inside that basket will make you gasp.

A jar is a fair guess, friend, but the angel names something else. He says, "A measuring basket is going forth." (Zechariah 5:6) A basket, not a jar. You'll see why that matters when the lid comes up.

A chest sounds like it could hold a secret, friend. But the angel says, "A measuring basket is going forth." (Zechariah 5:6) It's a basket, and it has a cover of lead on it. That's the thing to remember.
Yes, friend. The angel says, "This is Wickedness." (Zechariah 5:8) The woman sitting in the basket is named Wickedness. And she isn't sitting there for long.
Wisdom is a lovely name, friend, but that's not who's in there. The angel says, "This is Wickedness." (Zechariah 5:8) The two words start the same, so I understand the mix-up. It's Wickedness.
Jerusalem is a real city, friend, but the angel gives a different name. He says, "This is Wickedness." (Zechariah 5:8) The woman in the basket is Wickedness. The text doesn't call her a city.

explanations.answer: Shoves her down and shuts the lead cover
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The angel "shoved her down into the basket, pushing down the lead cover over its opening." (Zechariah 5:8) Down she goes and the lid comes down. Lead is heavy, so I think that lid isn't coming off easy.

explanations.answer: Lets her climb out and walk away free
explanations.explanation: No walking away for her, friend. The angel "shoved her down into the basket, pushing down the lead cover over its opening." (Zechariah 5:8) She goes down and the lid goes on. The lid is lead, so I think it's staying put.

explanations.answer: Hands the basket over to Zechariah
explanations.explanation: Zechariah doesn't get the basket, friend, and I think he's glad about that. The angel "shoved her down into the basket, pushing down the lead cover over its opening." (Zechariah 5:8) The angel handles it himself. Zechariah just watches.

explanations.answer: Lift it up between heaven and earth
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says the two women "lifted up the basket between heaven and earth." (Zechariah 5:9) They do it with wind in their wings. Up it goes, high in the air.

explanations.answer: Drop it down into the deep sea
explanations.explanation: Nothing gets dropped, friend. The text says the two women "lifted up the basket between heaven and earth." (Zechariah 5:9) They carry it up, not down. The sea isn't in this passage.

explanations.answer: Set it down by the temple gate
explanations.explanation: The temple gate is a good guess, friend, but they don't stop there. The text says the two women "lifted up the basket between heaven and earth." (Zechariah 5:9) They pick it up and carry it. They're headed somewhere else.

That's it, friend. The angel says, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar." (Zechariah 5:11) Shinar is the land where the basket is going. When it's ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal.

Goshen is a real place in the Bible, friend, but it's not this one. The angel says they're going "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar." (Zechariah 5:11) Shinar is the answer. That's where the basket will be set.

Moab is a real land too, friend, so I see why it came to mind. But the angel says, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar." (Zechariah 5:11) Shinar is where the basket is headed. A house gets built for it there.
